title: Vishvamitra takes the boys
hook: the verse that wakes Rama on his first morning away from home is still sung at dawn

segments.voice: Yesterday: Vishvamitra asked for Rama, a father pleaded, and the sage's anger shook the earth. Your line was Rama is not yet sixteen.

In many homes and temples in South India, the day starts with a recording of a Sanskrit hymn, the Venkatesha Suprabhatam, a song to wake the Lord at Tirupati. Its very first verse isn't new. It's borrowed, word for word, from the Ramayana: what Vishvamitra says to wake Rama on his first morning away from home, sleeping on grass by a river. But first, the boys have to leave.
screen: `A HYMN AT DAWN IN SOUTH INDIA.` → `ITS FIRST VERSE IS FROM THE RAMAYANA.` → `RAMA'S FIRST MORNING AWAY.`

segments.voice: Vasishtha, the royal priest, speaks to the frightened king. You've given your word, he says. Breaking it would undo all your merit. And Vishvamitra knows every divine weapon there is; Rama will be safer with him than anywhere. Dasharatha yields. He calls for Rama, and Lakshmana, who won't be left behind, and blesses them. The boys walk out after the sage, bows in hand, quivers on their backs, and the text says a soft breeze blew and flowers fell from the sky. After a day's walk, on the south bank of the Sarayu, Vishvamitra teaches Rama two mantras, bala and atibala, strength and great strength. With these, he says, you won't feel hunger or thirst or tiredness, and no one will match you, awake or asleep. That night the princes sleep on grass, like ordinary travelers. At dawn the sage wakes them: kausalya supraja rama purva sandhya pravartate, uttishtha narashardula kartavyam daivam ahnikam. Rama, fortunate son of Kausalya, the morning twilight is here. Rise, tiger among men; the day's sacred duties are waiting. The boys rise, bathe, say their prayers and walk on, to a hermitage where, the sage tells them, Shiva once burned Kama, the god of desire, to ash. They've left their father's house. Their teacher's world has begun.
screen: `VASISHTHA: KEEP YOUR WORD.` · `THE BOYS WALK OUT, FLOWERS FALL.` · `BALA AND ATIBALA BY THE RIVER.` · `A SAGE WAKES THEM AT DAWN.` · then, large: `KAUSALYĀ SUPRAJĀ RĀMA PŪRVĀ SANDHYĀ PRAVARTATE.`

segments.voice: Sit as if it's very early, the light just starting, and imagine a kind voice saying your name the way Vishvamitra said Rama's: not rushing you, just letting you know the day has come. On each breath in, rise a little; on each breath out, settle into the day you actually have.
Atibala, great strength, one of the two mantras Vishvamitra teaches Rama. Persuaded by Vasishtha, Dasharatha lets Rama and Lakshmana go, and the sage teaches them, and wakes them, on the road.
Your line: rise, tiger among men. The sage wakes him by name, gently, with the day's good work waiting. Day four hundred ninety-nine, done.

howItsDone: The Venkatesha Suprabhatam, sung at dawn at the Tirumala temple and played in many homes, opens with Vishvamitra's verse from the Bala Kanda waking Rama.

original.note: Sanskrit atibalā: great strength. with balā, strength, the two mantras Vishvamitra teaches Rama.

trapdoor: what you thought: the dawn hymn was written for the temple.
what it means: its opening verse is Vishvamitra's wake-up call to Rama, from the Bala Kanda.
what a scholar hears: Bala Kanda 23.2 opens the Venkatesha Suprabhatam; bala and atibala, given in sarga 22, are called daughters of Brahma in the text.

chat.says: Dasharatha begged to keep Rama home. Why did he let him go in the end?
options: Vasishtha reminded him he'd given his word, and Rama would be safe with the sage.
Rama slipped out at night, and the king couldn't catch him in time.
Vishvamitra promised to send him home within ten days, crowned and safe.
chat.meaning: Vasishtha told the king that breaking his word would undo his merit, and that Rama would be safer with Vishvamitra than anywhere.

Vasishtha.meaning: the royal priest of Dasharatha's court

atibala.meaning: great strength: a mantra against hunger, thirst and tiredness

Kausalya.meaning: Rama's mother, named in the sage's dawn verse
